references.text: Peter ran to the tomb and found it empty, just as the women had said. [ref:Luk 24:12|Luke 24:12] describes Peter's visit to the tomb, which is the event the travelers on the road to Emmaus are referring to here.

In [ref:Joh 20:3-10|John 20:3-10], it is told that Peter and the disciple whom Jesus loved ran to the tomb and found the burial cloths lying there, but not Jesus' body – they "found it just as the women had said, but him they did not see".

The women went to the tomb early in the morning and found the stone rolled away, but Jesus' body was gone. [ref:Luk 24:1-3|Luke 24:1-3] is the original account that is being retold here by the travelers on the road to Emmaus.

In [ref:Luk 24:22-23|Luke 24:22-23], the travelers on the road to Emmaus tell about the women's testimony concerning the empty tomb and the vision of angels, which verse 24 is a direct continuation of.
In [ref:Mark 16:5-6|Mark 16:5-6], the women find the tomb empty and meet an angel who says that Jesus has risen – they found it just as described, but they did not see Jesus himself.
Mary Magdalene found the tomb empty and ran to tell Peter and the other disciple ([ref:Joh 20:1-2|John 20:1-2]), which led the disciples themselves to go and confirm the women's account.
